subject: Quarterly review: infra capacity & unit-economics synthesis
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quarterly review: infra capacity & unit-economics synthesis

Team —

Ahead of the leadership quarterly review I'm consolidating the infra capacity + unit economics narrative. The goal is a one-page ask for leadership: what committed capacity we need, what it costs, and the operational mitigations (batching, caching, quantization) that materially change unit economics.

Please send me the following by EOD Wed 16 Jun (hard deadline so I can lock the deck):
- Marcus: baseline fleet state + utilization histograms (last 90 days), peak-day demand, and 95/99p latency vs cost tradeoffs. Attach any spreadsheets.
- Monica: three forecast scenarios (baseline growth, customer pilot surge, high-growth) with recommended buffer policy and autoscale knobs.
- Vivek: ask in $ committed (1, 6, 12 month options) and quick ROI calc vs on-demand.
- Aditya: I'll need the leadership slide skeleton updated with the ask box (slide 6) — I'll drop figures once numbers are final.

Context: AtlasAI pilot (Matt Johnson) is going live in Q3; their initial signal could increase peak concurrency by ~15-25% for a short window. We need to show we can absorb that without SLA erosion or disproportionate cost.

Attachments: capacity_model_v3.xlsx (working model)

Thanks — short bullets and numbers please, not prose.

Olga Petrov
Director, Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly review: infra capacity & unit-economics synthesis

Olga —

Attached: capacity_model_v3.xlsx (sheet 'utilization') + quick notes below. High level numbers from last 90 days:
- Fleet (A100-equivalent): 320 GPUs (mix of p4/p5/A100 normalized).
- Average utilization (weighted): 42% overall.
- 95th percentile sustained utilization: 68%. 99th: 78% (short bursts).
- Tokens/sec per GPU (baseline, small-batch): ~3.4k tokens/s. With continuous batching (our inferred policy) we see effective tokens/s increase to ~6.1k (+1.8x).
- Prefix/KV caching observed reductions: repeated-context workloads show ~12% token reduction across the dataset; high-similarity customers see 20-30%.

Implications:
- To meet 99th-percentile demand with our current model mix we need ~80 spare GPUs if we keep the same batching/caching profile. If we can increase batching (larger latency budget) we can reduce that delta by ~25 GPUs.
- For a 1-month surge (Atlas pilot style) with peak day at +25% we have enough headroom for short windows if burst autoscaling is configured (but costs spike on on-demand).

Attachments: capacity_model_v3.xlsx (contains per-day utilization, peak-day sim).

-Marcus
Senior Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly review: infra capacity & unit-economics synthesis

Olga / Marcus —

I ran three forecast scenarios in the attached sim: batching-sim-results.csv (columns: scenario, required_gpus, peak_concurrency, expected_cost_delta). High-level:
1) Conservative (baseline growth +10%): require +40 GPUs buffer, preferred approach: modest reserved commit (3-month) + auto-scale floor.
2) Pilot surge (baseline +25% peak days for 4 weeks): require +70-85 GPUs on peak days; combine short-term on-demand burst + canary routing (route non-critical traffic to quantized variants) to flatten SLA risk.
3) Aggressive (50% sustained growth): need re-architecting of batching/caching + ~180 GPUs more; recommend immediate purchase of reserved capacity at a blended discount.

Autoscale notes: set burst target to 1.2x baseline PU with fast spin-up (under 5 minutes) for stateless requesters; for stateful KV-heavy flows increase spin-up to handle checkpoint warmup.

I'll flag that increasing average batch size by 25% reduces required GPUs by ~20% in scenario 2, but adds ~15-40ms tail latency depending on model.

-Monica
Staff PM, Capacity Planning
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly review: infra capacity & unit-economics synthesis

Thanks — quick financial read and recommendation.

Cost inputs (normalized):
- On-demand GPU-hour (A100-eq): $3.60/hr
- Committed (3m): $2.70/hr (25% discount)
- Committed (12m): $2.16/hr (40% discount)
- Opportunity cost: model reprovisioning & migration ~1-2 days of eng time per 100 GPUs.

Simple ROI (scenario 2, pilot surge):
- If we reserve 80 GPUs for 3 months: monthly commit cost delta vs on-demand ~ (3.60-2.70)*24*30*80 = $155,520 saved vs on-demand for that capacity over the month (gross).
- Payback: we need ~1.5 months of steady utilization to justify a 3m commit vs repeated on-demand bursts.

Operational mitigations I recommend we bake into the ask:
1) Commit to a conservative 3-month reserve for 80 GPUs (covers 99p spikes + pilot buffer) and reevaluate 6 weeks after pilot start.
2) Canary routing: route 25% of pilot traffic to quantized / 8-bit variants (reduces token cost ~30%); escalate to 50% if quality holds.
3) Temporary cross-region failover: use eu-us spill for overflow if local capacity exhausted (higher network cost but avoids SLA misses).

Ask for leadership: approval to sign a 3-month $X commit (ops will provide exact contract), plus authority to apply canary routing on pilot start.

-Vivek
VP, Infrastructure Operations

Subject: Re: Quarterly review: infra capacity & unit-economics synthesis — final ask and owners

Team — thanks for the fast turn. Final synthesis and ask below (this will be the box I put in the leadership deck):

Final ask (one-liner): Approve a 3-month reserved commit for 80 GPUs to cover 99p demand and AtlasAI pilot buffer; authorize canary routing to quantized variants for up to 25% of pilot traffic.

Why: 
- Current fleet requires ~80 spare GPUs to meet 99p spikes (Marcus).
- Pilot could add up to +25% peak concurrency for short windows (Monica + Atlas).
- 3m commit materially reduces unit cost and is payback-positive if utilization holds for the pilot window (Vivek).

Action items & owners (target dates):
- Finance: prepare 3m commit contract options and nominal $ values (Vivek) — DUE: 2027-06-22
- Runtime: finalize batching tuning and KV cache warmup playbook; present tail-latency impact and mitigation (Marcus) — DUE: 2027-06-21
- Capacity PM: confirm autoscale floor and burst policy; include regional failover runbook (Monica) — DUE: 2027-06-21
- Product: finalize slide visuals and ask wording (Aditya) — DUE: 2027-06-18 (completed; please confirm)
- AtlasAI: confirm pilot schedule and canary cohort (Matt / procurement) — DUE: 2027-06-24

I'll fold this into the leadership deck and circulate the final PDF by Monday EOD. If anyone objects to the ask or has a material concern, raise it now — otherwise I'll proceed.

Olga Petrov
Director, Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference
